title: SOC triage: workstation
summary: A crypto miner disguised as a kernel worker runs from /tmp and restarts from a user systemd unit. Disconnect from the network and save the evidence before you clean anything.

panels.title: Suspicious
panels.note: Investigate first. Do not kill yet: you would lose the evidence.
rows: Named `kworkerd` to look like a kernel thread, but has an executable: `/tmp/.x/kworkerd (deleted)`. Uses 380% CPU and holds a connection to 203.0.113.7:3333, a common mining pool port.
`~/.config/systemd/user/kworkerd.service` was created 2 days ago and starts the same binary at login.

panels.title: Junk to clean
panels.note: Safe to stop. You run the commands.
rows: headless Chromium from an old test run

panels.title: Odd but yours
panels.note: Not a threat. Confirm you started these.
rows: Has been listening on 127.0.0.1:5037 for 2 days. Stop it with `adb kill-server` if you are done with your phone.
An out-of-tree module is loaded: the NVIDIA driver. Expected on this machine.

cards.title: low LLMNR (local-network name lookup)
cards.body: When DNS cannot find a name, systemd-resolved asks the whole local network and answers others on port 5355. Anyone on the same Wi-Fi can answer first and send you to a fake host. You almost never need it. To undo, delete no-llmnr.conf and restart systemd-resolved.
